name: Teladoc Health
one_liner: Video or phone therapy and psychiatry from licensed US clinicians, usually through an employer or health plan; self-pay visits are also offered.
best_for: People whose employer or health plan includes Teladoc mental health benefits
Adults who want therapy and psychiatric medication management in one service
People who prefer paying per visit rather than a monthly subscription
Teens 13–17 covered as dependents who need therapy (not psychiatry)
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988, or call 911
Teens who need psychiatric medication (psychiatry is adults only)
People who need intensive programs such as partial hospitalization or residential care
short_description: Per-visit video or phone therapy and psychiatry, mostly through employer or health-plan benefits, with self-pay visits available.
long_description: Teladoc Health is a US virtual care company whose mental health service offers scheduled therapy with licensed therapists and psychiatry (evaluation and medication management) with psychiatrists and psychiatric providers, by video or phone. Most members get access through an employer, health plan or other benefit program, which determines the cost. People without Teladoc benefits or without insurance can still register and pay per visit; Teladoc's mental health page lists self-pay prices of $95 for therapy, $235 for a first psychiatry visit and $105 for psychiatry follow-ups, while its billing FAQ gives ranges up to $119 for therapy and $299/$129 for psychiatry, so the price shown before you confirm a visit is the one that applies. Teens 13–17 can see a therapist as eligible dependents, with a parent or guardian present at the start and end of the first visit; psychiatry is not offered to that age group. Teladoc also offers a self-guided digital mental health program (formerly myStrength) only through qualifying employer or health-plan benefits. Teladoc owns BetterHelp, which is a separate subscription service. It is not a crisis service.
patient_summary: Teladoc Health connects you with a licensed therapist or psychiatrist by video or phone, scheduled through its app or website. Most people get it as a benefit from an employer or health plan, which sets what you pay (often a copay); if you don't have it as a benefit you can still book and pay per visit. Psychiatry and medication are for adults; teens 13–17 can get therapy as eligible dependents with a parent present at the first visit.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with employer or insurance benefit; $95/session therapy self-pay
pricing.notes: Self-pay prices on Teladoc's mental health page: therapy $95/visit, first psychiatry visit $235, psychiatry follow-up $105. Teladoc's billing FAQ lists ranges of $0–$119 for therapy, $0–$299 for a first psychiatry visit and $0–$129 for follow-ups; the exact fee is shown before you confirm a visit. HSA/FSA/HRA cards accepted on eligible plans. No subscription.

privacy.notes: Clinical records are HIPAA-protected; the website privacy policy says it uses targeting cookies and shares identifiers with advertising partners (opt-out offered). No regulator action against Teladoc found; its subsidiary BetterHelp has a 2023 FTC order.

seo.title: Teladoc Health: Largest US Telehealth Platform | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Teladoc offers 24/7 video therapy and psychiatry with typical wait times under 5 minutes, covered by most insurance plans.

faqs.q: Is Teladoc therapy covered by my insurance?
faqs.a: Most commercial insurance and employer plans cover Teladoc mental health services. Check your benefits portal or call the number on your insurance card. Typical copays are $0-75 per visit. Many employers offer Teladoc at no cost as a benefit.

faqs.q: How quickly can I see a Teladoc therapist?
faqs.a: Teladoc offers both on-demand and scheduled visits. On-demand therapy typically connects you within 5-15 minutes. Scheduled visits with a consistent therapist are available within 1-2 weeks. Psychiatry appointments typically require scheduling.

Teladoc psychiatrists can prescribe ADHD medications including controlled substances in most states, though policies vary. Initial evaluations are required before prescribing. Teladoc follows DEA telehealth prescribing guidelines and state regulations.

faqs.q: How is Teladoc different from BetterHelp?
faqs.a: Teladoc acquired BetterHelp in 2022. Teladoc typically comes through employer/insurance benefits with copay-based pricing. BetterHelp is direct-to-consumer with subscription pricing. If your employer offers Teladoc, that's usually the more affordable option.

primary_uses: Video or phone therapy for anxiety, depression and stress

availability.note: US. Therapy for adults and teens 13–17 (as eligible dependents); psychiatry adults only. Usually via employer or health-plan benefits; self-pay visits available.
